candidate.title: Quartz-seq2
candidate.scope: The independent middle Quartz-seq2 row of the assigned Illumina poster crop, from single-cell sorting and poly(A)-RNA reverse transcription through early cDNA pooling, TdT poly(A) tagging, second-strand synthesis and the broad amplification/custom-library block. The crop also shows separate neighboring Quartz-Seq and DP-Seq rows; their independent labels and routes, together with the assigned card title, identify them as surrounding poster context rather than alternative targets of this card. No inter-row transfer or interchangeable implementation is asserted. Primary-paper detail clarifies the custom library and readout interfaces without expanding unshown execution steps or alternative library preparations.

states.label: Single cell with polyadenylated RNA
features: Biological target is polyadenylated cellular RNA, illustrated as PolyA RNA; the final sequenced material will be DNA copies.
The PolyA RNA icon identifies the target within the single-cell workflow; it does not specify a separate RNA purification or poly(A)-selection operation.

states.label: Sequencing-ready cDNA-derived DNA library
features: Depicted as multiple short adapter-ended DNA molecules; the final product is not RNA.
Library molecules retain a transcript-derived sequence physically associated with a cell barcode and UMI; sequencing adapters and pool barcodes are added.
For the paper-supported custom library implementation, P5 and P7 are flow-cell interfaces; Read1 reads cell barcode plus UMI, Index1 reads pool barcode, and Read2 reads transcript sequence.

Transcript sequence provides gene association, the cell barcode identifies the source cell, and the UMI supports transcript counting with reduced PCR-duplication bias. Counts describe captured and successfully converted polyadenylated RNA, not guaranteed recovery of every RNA molecule.
Pool barcodes permit different sets of cell-barcoded cDNA to be mixed; a second physical pooling operation is not depicted.

evidence.locator: Middle row, Amplify & custom library prep arrow to cDNA library ready for sequencing; caption specifies sequencing adapters and pool barcodes

evidence.quote: Such fragmented cDNA is ligated with a truncated Y-shaped sequence adaptor, which has an Illumina flow-cell binding sequence (P7) and a pool barcode sequence (PB). The PB makes it possible to mix different sets of cell barcode-labeled cDNA.
Ligated cDNA, which has CB and MB sequences, is enriched by PCR amplification. The resulting sequence library DNA contains P7 and P5 flow-cell binding sequences at respective ends of the DNA.
We sequence the cell barcode site and the UMI site at Read1, the pool barcode site at Index1, and the transcript sequence at Read2.
Finally, the UMI for each gene for each cell was counted using DigitalExpression of Drop-seq tools, which generated the digital expression matrix.

operations.label: Single-cell in PCR well plate
operations.description: Sort individual cells into separate PCR wells containing lysis buffer and RT primers; the material changes from a cell before placement to single-cell material in a defined well.
operations.mechanism: The depicted caption specifies sorting; the primary paper identifies cell sorting by flow cytometry into PCR wells.
operations.information_effect: Well separation permits subsequent assignment of one RT-primer cell barcode to the RNA from each cell. The PolyA RNA icon is target identification within this stage.

evidence.locator: Middle row, left: Single cell, PolyA RNA, Single-cell in PCR well plate; caption states single cells are sorted into PCR wells containing lysis buffer and RT primers

evidence.quote: Each single cell in a droplet is sorted into lysis buffer in each well of a 384-well PCR plate using flow cytometry analysis data.

operations.label: Lysis & RT
operations.description: Lyse the well-associated cell and reverse-transcribe its polyadenylated RNA using the barcode/UMI-bearing oligo(dT) primer, producing first-strand cDNA shown in an RNA/cDNA duplex.
operations.mechanism: Oligo(dT) priming on RNA poly(A) couples reverse transcription to incorporation of the primer-borne cell barcode, UMI and PCR sequence.
operations.information_effect: Transfers transcript sequence information from RNA into DNA and attaches cell and molecule identifiers before samples are physically combined.

evidence.locator: Middle row, Lysis & RT arrow and mRNA/cDNA duplex; oligo-dT segment, Cell barcode, UMI, PCR primer labels

evidence.quote: Each well contains lysis buffer and reverse-transcription (RT) primer, which includes a cell barcode sequence (14- or 15-mer), a UMI sequence (8-mer), and an oligo-dT sequence (24-mer).
Using these RT primers, respective RNA from single cells is converted to cDNA with unique cell barcodes.

operations.label: Pool & purify
operations.description: Combine cDNA-containing material from the individual wells and purify it for whole-transcript amplification. The input collection of separate well-specific preparations becomes a common first-strand cDNA preparation.
operations.mechanism: The caption combines pooling and purification; it does not specify the internal purification sequence at this schematic scope.
operations.information_effect: Physical well separation ends, while the cDNA-linked cell barcode preserves cell-of-origin association and the UMI stays with each copied transcript.

evidence.locator: Middle row, Pool & purify arrow from individually labeled cDNA to pooled WTA material

evidence.quote: The third step involves the pooling of cell-barcoded cDNA.
Collected first-strand cDNAs are purified and concentrated for subsequent whole-transcript amplification.

operations.label: PolyA tail synthesized by TdT enzyme
operations.description: Extend pooled, purified first-strand cDNA with an artificial poly(A) tail, creating a new primer-binding tract on the cDNA.
operations.mechanism: Terminal deoxynucleotidyl transferase adds the poly(A) tail to first-strand DNA.
operations.information_effect: Adds an amplification interface while retaining transcript, cell-barcode and UMI associations; the artificial DNA tail is distinct from biological RNA poly(A). The figure’s 3.6-fold annotation is interpreted as the amplified-cDNA yield improvement measured for the combined poly(A)-tagging improvements, rather than a direct 3.6-fold UMI-conversion effect of TdT alone (see correction c_tagging_metric).

evidence.quote: Poly(A) tagging is composed of two processes: (1) the first-strand cDNA is modified with a poly(A) tail by terminal deoxynucleotidyl transferase; and (2) the poly(A)-tailed cDNA is annealed with a tagging primer, which has a poly(dT) sequence.
Moreover, upon combining T55 buffer and the Increment condition, the amount of cDNA increased approximately 3.6-fold.

operations.label: 2nd strand synthesis
operations.description: Anneal the PCR-sequence-bearing poly(dT) tagging primer to the artificial cDNA poly(A) tail and extend it to generate second-strand cDNA with PCR priming sequences at both ends.
operations.mechanism: Poly(dT)-directed tagging-primer extension copies the first-strand DNA; the primer supplies the additional PCR priming sequence.
operations.information_effect: Converts tagged first-strand cDNA into an amplifiable product without creating a new cell identity or UMI.

evidence.locator: Middle row, arrow to PCR primer with polyT tail and dashed 2nd strand synthesis extension over A-tailed first-strand cDNA

evidence.quote: Poly(A) tagging is composed of two processes: (1) the first-strand cDNA is modified with a poly(A) tail by terminal deoxynucleotidyl transferase; and (2) the poly(A)-tailed cDNA is annealed with a tagging primer, which has a poly(dT) sequence.
Then, the second-strand cDNA is extended. The resulting second-strand cDNA is amplifiable cDNA, which has a PCR primer sequence at both ends of it.

operations.label: Amplify & custom library prep
operations.description: Amplify the second-strand cDNA product and convert it into the adapter-bearing, pool-barcoded DNA library depicted as ready for sequencing. Keep this as the single broad block shown.
operations.mechanism: The depicted block combines amplification and custom library construction. The matched primary paper clarifies that this custom implementation fragments amplified cDNA, ligates a truncated Y-shaped sequencing adapter carrying a pool barcode, and enriches barcode/UMI-bearing fragments by PCR; these are not extra local operations in the graph.
operations.information_effect: Produces library DNA linking a transcript-derived sequence to its original cell barcode and UMI, and introduces pool identity and Illumina sequencing interfaces. Read1 supplies cell/UMI identity, Index1 supplies pool identity and Read2 supplies transcript identity, supporting gene-level UMI counts per cell. Sequencing and downstream counting are explanatory readout interfaces, not additional depicted operations.

method_scopes.rationale: All listed local operations belong to the explicitly labeled middle row and match the Quartz-Seq2 outline and Figure 1 in Sasagawa et al. (2018). Quartz-seq2/Quartz-Seq2 are capitalization variants of this version name. The cell-barcode/UMI route is distinct from the separate neighboring Quartz-Seq and DP-Seq routes. In particular, their primer-digestion, blocking-primer/suppression-PCR or designed-heptamer operations do not belong to this local route. The paper describes more than one library preparation, but the depicted adapter/pool-barcode custom-library block is interpreted using its Figure 1 custom-ligation implementation.

corrections.diagram_observation: The middle-row WTA caption reads: WTA using terminal deoxynucleotidyl transferase (TdT) provides 3.6 fold increase in polyA tagging to UMI conversion efficiency. Its wording can be read as attributing a 3.6-fold increase directly to UMI conversion or to TdT alone.
corrections.primary_statement: The primary paper reports approximately 3.6-fold greater amplified cDNA yield for the combination of improved tailing-buffer and tagging/second-strand conditions. It treats improved poly(A) tagging as contributing to higher UMI conversion, but the 3.6-fold measurement is not itself a direct measurement of a TdT-only UMI-conversion increase. The route and depicted TdT tailing are retained; o_tail explicitly uses the paper-supported metric interpretation.

checks.rationale: The assigned middle row is represented completely at its depicted resolution: single-cell placement, lysis/RT, pooling/purification, TdT tailing, tagging-primer second-strand synthesis, and broad amplification/custom library preparation. All states and material routes agree with their receiving operations and Quartz-seq2 scope. Barcode/UMI identity survives pooling and library construction. The only two-input operation joins a primer to its template; no independently processed branches are collapsed. Adjacent workflows are context. The paper association, readout interface and explicit metric correction are supported by the inspected full-text passages and captions; no consequential unknown remains.
